title: How do I make custom outfits? ( Sprite only)

posts.author: sad-little_doll
posts.body:
Hi! I'm somewhat new to RPG Maker. I was wondering how I could go about making a different outfit for my sprites? I'd like the sprites to match my image renders as closely as possible and thought I could do the pixel art myself, but I'm finding it challenging, especially since I'd have to copy and paste the same outfit onto like 20 characters.
Any help would be so appreciated!

posts.author: Deleted member 222036
posts.body: maybe it can help with copy and pasting, but when i need to copy n paste alot i tend to kinda multiply it. like, i put it on one character, then i duplicate the layer and merge it to the one below, then i duplicate that layer and now the image covers two sprites! maybe this is confusing and not what your looking for, but i hope it helps

posts.author: TeiRaven
posts.body:
The easiest way to start in sprite work is "frankenspriting," where you take existing pieces and put them together rather than doing everything completely from scratch. For example: you can take the hair from one sprite, make it the color of a different sprite, take the outfit from a third and and recolor it. The result will be completely different from any of the pieces used to make it. Avery has a great tutorial on frankenspiting--I don't have the link to hand, but look in the General Tutorials section, I hink it's there!
As far as making lots of sprites being a lot of work: yeah, it is. No way around that. But there are a couple things you can look into for speeding up your workflow.
First, the built-in generator. I don't know how to make generator parts for MV/Z, but you could look into that for speeding up the "same outfit on 20 different characters" process. If you have Game Character Hub, you could import that outfit into your library and use it similarly--you just need the image of only the outfit, the Import process will take care of the rest.
I do all my sprites in GIMP. As with all things, it goes faster once you get the workflow down. I was making students in uniforms just last night, actually. I made one sprite wearing the uniform, them duplicated the layer and removed the original student's head. I made the other students by duplicating the uniform base and adding different heads (and adjusting the color of the hands to match the skintone of the face, if they're different).

posts.author: JohnDoeGames
posts.body: I just put a "naked" character from the character generator in a sheet, then put a layer on top of it, to draw the clothing in. Then I delete the bottom layer, so I end up with the clothing only.

posts.author: sad-little_doll
posts.body: Thank you all so so so much! This was all very helpful! I think I have a pretty good grasp on how to go about it now, I'll just save it for later since it seems like it's going to be a very involved process.

posts.author: ShardsUnremebered40
posts.body:
if you know how to layer images from put together pieces this is how you can do it:
- 1. Layer 1 - base model, (make hair separate layer to position it)
- 2. Layer 2 - the style (clothing + accessories)
- 3. Layer 3 - the artist's touch. [add your own pixels here]
Or, there is another way altogether more riskier, drawing on the base sprite itself!
(not recommended for everyone)

posts.author: TheAM-Dol
posts.body:
If you want the sprite to change according to the armor they are wearing, you likely want to look into a Paper Doll plugin.
Basically, what this is a "doll", that you can apply sprites ontop of and in sync with the doll.
So in a sense you don't have to create the same sprite but wearing different clothes, you just create the nude sprite, and then create a clothes sprite, and the plugin will apply it the nude sprite based on conditions (which depends on the plugin)
I haven't looked into paper doll plugins, so I don't have any recommendations for you, but hopefully the term "paper doll" gets you closer to what you are looking for in your google search.
